title: Decoding Browsing and Selection Intentions in Gaze Interaction Based on Gaze Related Potentials and Eye Movement Features
content: Gaze-controlled interfaces must distinguish inspection from intended selection without relying on measurements acquired after the decision deadline. This study evaluates prefix-limited condition decoding from fixation-related potentials (FRPs), derived from electroencephalography (EEG), and logged eye-event timing. Prefix-aligned calibrated fusion (PACF) combines participant-cross-fitted branch scores, independent-participant probability calibration, and confidence-based deferral. Public mixed-reality data provide instructed Select and Observe conditions; 118 of 192 fixed candidates from eight participants pass availability and sampling-quality checks. At a reconstructed 350 ms horizon, mean participant area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) is 0.513 for gaze timing, 0.543 for FRPs, 0.576 for early fusion, and 0.504 for PACF. Calibration increases PACF Brier error from 0.245 to 0.252, while confidence rejection reduces coverage without improving accepted accuracy. Severe voltage excursions, differential attrition, and uncertain timing constrain interpretation. The study supports an offline feasibility audit with transparent negative fusion results, rather than unrestricted browsing discrimination or real-time command activation.
